issues.title: Terminal-regime tracking uses the lemma outside its stated domain

failure_location.quote:
Apply the finite-horizon tracking estimate
Eq.~\eqref{eq:finite_horizon_tracking_rho} with $T=N$ and $\rho/2$

issues.failure_explanation: The finite-horizon estimate requires x_t∈K for all perturbed points and uses uniform continuity of f on K. In the application K is set to [−1,1], while compactness of the certificate sublevel establishes only a uniform bound on L_t. The ellipse relation even permits |L| up to 2/δ for δ<2, so membership in [−1,1] does not follow. Thus the estimate was invoked without its trajectory-domain hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The terminal-case step establishing entry into the attracting residual neighborhood was incomplete for both rank-1 factorization and rank-1 approximation pre-critical convergence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the tracking result for a continuous map on ℝ and a perturbed orbit contained in a compact set C. For each finite horizon T, use uniform continuity on the compact set C_T=⋃_{j=0}^T f^j(C). In both terminal-regime applications, take C to be the compact image of the already invariant certificate sublevel set under the residual map, rather than assuming that every finite residual lies in [−1,1], and then apply the same entry-and-trapping argument.
issues.why_classification: The old application genuinely violates a lemma hypothesis, so this is not a typo. However, compactness of the full trajectory is already available, and extending the finite-horizon estimate to the resulting compact residual set is a standard local uniform-continuity repair. It preserves both affected convergence theorems without weakening their scope or conclusions.

issues.title: Strict inwardness proof omits the zero-coefficient equality case

failure_location.quote:
If $4\|a_t\|^2-\delta\ge 0$, then $r_t(\delta)\ge 0$ is obvious.
Therefore, we only consider the case $4\|a_t\|^2-\delta<0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Nonnegativity of r_t is insufficient because the proposition claims R_t^apx<0 at every nonstationary boundary point. The old proof did not exclude r_t=0 when 4‖a_t‖²−δ=0. Under R_t^apx=0 and q_η(δ)<0, the missing case forces D_t^S=0 and L_t=0; the boundary identity then gives v_t²=−δ/4, which is impossible.
issues.overall_effect: The strict boundary-inward proposition, and hence the strictness input used by the rank-1 approximation convergence theorem, had an unclosed equality case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split the case 4‖a_t‖²−δ≥0 into strict and equality cases. In the equality case, if R_t^apx=0, then q_η(δ)<0 forces D_t^S=0 and r_t(δ)=0 forces L_t=0. Parallelism and ⟨a_t,b_t⟩=1 then give ‖b_t‖²=4/δ, while the boundary identity yields v_t²=−δ/4, a contradiction. The strict positive case gives equality only at a global minimizer. This completes strict inwardness and leaves the dependent convergence theorem unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Strictness requires a genuine missing equality-case argument, but the contradiction is a short local algebraic check using formulas already present in the proof. No new lemma, hypothesis, or weakening of the proposition or dependent theorem is needed.

issues.title: Finite numerical traces do not establish unbounded growth

failure_location.quote:
In fact, unlike the rank-1 factorization case — where GD converges on a
balanced manifold throughout $\eta \in (1, 2)$ — no such convergence
appears in the rank-1 approximation setting: numerical experiments show
that the norms $\|a_t\|^2 + \|b_t\|^2 + u_t^2 + v_t^2$ grow without bound
(Figure~\ref{fig:main_post_critical}), even within the narrower range
$\eta \in (1, \sqrt{5} - 1)$ in which the factorization dynamics lock onto
a $2$-cycle.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
We then track the
norm $\|a_t\|^2 + \|b_t\|^2 + u_t^2 + v_t^2$ for $T = 600$ iterations.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that numerical experiments show the approximation norm grows without bound, an asymptotic assertion. The old paper actually computes trajectories for T=600 iterations and therefore establishes only rapid growth or finite-horizon blow-up in the plotted runs. The material difference is that eventual unboundedness is not distinguished from a long transient or a large bounded orbit by those experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The empirical comparison with factorization remains informative, but the remark and figure caption overstate it as an asymptotic divergence conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Revise the remark, figure captions, and associated experimental discussion to state only that the tested trajectories exhibit rapid norm growth after a transient over the plotted T=600 iterations. Remove assertions that the experiments show unboundedness or asymptotic divergence, and present the absence of stabilization as finite-horizon numerical evidence rather than an established limit statement.
issues.why_classification: Replacing unbounded growth by rapid growth over a finite horizon changes the claim's asymptotic quantifier and therefore entails meaningful mathematical weakening, so a minor classification is inadequate. The weakening is nevertheless limited: the empirical factorization-versus-approximation comparison remains recognizably intact, no formal result depends on it, and only local prose changes are required.

issues.title: Uniqueness theorem wrongly includes the stationarity threshold endpoint

failure_location.quote:
Then $P(\delta)$ is uniquely determined for every
$\delta \in [\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta), \overline\delta)$.

issues.failure_explanation: At the canonical scalar threshold δ_th(η)=η, take b=0 and a²=(4−η²)/η. This is a certificate-boundary point with nonzero gradient. Nevertheless, the factor δ−η in R_t^sca makes the one-step certificate change zero, contradicting the axiom that equality occurs only at stationary points. Consistently, the old uniqueness proof fixes δ only in (δ_th(η), overline δ), so it does not establish the theorem's closed endpoint.
issues.overall_effect: The characterization is unsupported exactly at the threshold; the open nonterminal range and all strictly certified applications remain available.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the stationarity axiom and the uniqueness conclusion to δ∈(δ_th(η),overline δ). At δ=δ_th(η), retain at most the weak monotonicity statement and explicitly make no stationarity-equality or uniqueness assertion, since nonstationary boundary points can have zero one-step certificate change there.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine endpoint defect rather than a transcription-only error, because the stationarity axiom is false at the endpoint. The repair excludes only one degenerate threshold value, agrees with the proof's already open domain, and leaves the full strict nonterminal range and all applications unchanged.

issues.title: Uniqueness proof lacks level-minimizer coverage

failure_location.quote:
Thus the unbalanced minimizers sweep out the full
nonterminal parameter range $(0,2)$. Consequently, every nonterminal level set
compatible with Axioms~\ref{cond:P_is_pd}--\ref{cond:symmetry} is forced to coincide with the corresponding
level set of the family above.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: whenever a nonterminal level set contains an unbalanced global minimizer

issues.failure_explanation: The old proof determines a quadratic form only when the particular nonterminal boundary already contains an unbalanced global minimizer. It never establishes that premise for each level of the arbitrary family under consideration. Varying a minimizer through the canonical formula does not imply that every arbitrary level is met by one. The new proof first places a global minimizer in each compact forward-invariant level and then uses strict nesting to obtain an unbalanced boundary minimizer.
issues.overall_effect: Without the missing coverage step, only a conditional local uniqueness statement is proved; global uniqueness across all nonterminal levels is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a level-coverage argument before applying the local Lagrange calculation. In the concretely supported pre-critical route, state η∈(0,1), prove that each compact nonterminal K_δ is forward invariant, choose a generic interior trajectory, and use scalar GD convergence and closedness of K_δ to place a global minimizer in it. Then use strict nesting and compactness of the minimizer branch to obtain an unbalanced global minimizer on ∂K_δ. Applying the existing local calculation at that boundary point determines every nonterminal level.
issues.why_classification: The missing premise cannot be supplied by a routine edit: it requires a contained but nontrivial coverage lemma using forward invariance, convergence, and strict nesting. This restores a global level-by-level uniqueness result while retaining the original local Lagrange mechanism; the established η∈(0,1) version remains recognizably comparable, so neither global reconstruction nor major mathematical loss is unavoidable.

issues.title: Exact state-indexed uniqueness fails under monotone reparameterization

failure_location.quote:
With state space
$(0, 2]$, the unique family is

issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims numerical uniqueness of P(δ) on the original δ-scale. For example, fix η=1/2, let h(δ)=δ²/2 on (0,2], and set P_h(δ)=P_can(h(δ)). Choosing the admissible threshold δ_th=3/2 ensures h(δ)>η throughout the threshold range. Positive definiteness, strict nesting, terminal negligibility, the state assignment, symmetry, and boundary monotonicity/stationarity are preserved, but P_h(δ) differs from P_can(δ). Thus the axioms identify the normalized level-set family only up to an increasing change of state coordinate.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed ellipsoid family remains structurally distinguished, but its numerical parameterization is not uniquely determined by the old axioms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem as uniqueness up to an increasing reparameterization of the state coordinate. Explicitly assert that for every admissible family there is a strictly increasing map h such that P(δ)=P_can(h(δ)), with h(δ) tending to 2 at the terminal endpoint. If the displayed canonical formula is desired with the same symbol as its argument, first adopt ζ=h(δ) as the normalized state coordinate. Do not claim h(δ)=δ without an additional normalization axiom.
issues.why_classification: The old axioms admit genuinely different numerical parameterizations, so exact state-indexed uniqueness must be weakened or supported by a new normalization condition. Uniqueness of the nested ellipsoid family and its terminal geometry survives, making the loss limited rather than major, and the required reparameterization argument is contained. The issue therefore exceeds minor but does not require serious global reconstruction.

issues.title: Approximation robustness incorrectly includes q=0

failure_location.quote:
The step-size robustness in
Remark~\ref{rmk:inward_with_stepsize_le_delta} also holds beyond the scalar
setting: by Propositions~\ref{prop:boundary_inward_rank1}
and~\ref{prop:boundary_inward_rank1_approx}, for any point on the level set
$\{\ifac(\delta_t;\,\cdot)=0\}$ or $\{\iapx(\delta_t;\,\cdot)=0\}$, a GD step
with any step size $\eta'\in(0,\delta_t)$ maps the iterate strictly into the
interior of the corresponding sublevel set (for $\iapx$, additionally
requiring $q_{\eta'}(\delta_t)\le 0$).

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims strict interior mapping for rank-1 approximation whenever q_{η′}(δ_t)≤0. The cited formal proposition establishes strictness only for q_{η′}(δ_t)<0. At q=0, choose η′=4δ/(δ²+4), u=v=0, nonparallel signal vectors with inner product 1 and squared norms summing to 4/δ. The point is on the certificate boundary and is nonstationary, while L=N=0 and R^{apx}=η′q_{η′}(δ)D^S=0. Thus the endpoint gives equality rather than strict inwardness.
issues.overall_effect: Only the remark's endpoint robustness claim fails; the formal boundary-inward proposition and convergence theorem already use the correct strict condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Revise the approximation part of the remark to distinguish the endpoint: q_{η′}(δ_t)<0 gives strict mapping into the interior, while q_{η′}(δ_t)=0 guarantees at most membership in the closed sublevel set and can attain equality at a nonstationary point. Keep the factorization statement unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The endpoint assertion is genuinely false, but it concerns only the exceptional zero set of q and has no dependent formal result; the proposition and convergence theorem already use the correct strict condition. A short local qualification preserves the regular-regime robustness claim and even retains valid non-strict endpoint inwardness.
